_comment: Seccomp profile for claw-sandbox. Loaded by Docker via --security-opt seccomp=seccomp.json or by container runtimes that accept OCI-format profiles. Default action is SCMP_ACT_ALLOW so userspace works normally; the explicit denylist below blocks kernel-control surfaces an LLM-driven Coder has no business touching. Architectures match Docker's default profile.
_source: Distilled from Docker's default profile (https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/profiles/seccomp/default.json) plus the additional denials documented in claw-squad/docs/sandbox-hardening.md.

syscalls._comment: Process introspection / debugger surface. ptrace lets one process read another's memory; an LLM-generated Coder dropping a debugger into the sandbox is almost always a mistake or an attack.
Kernel module manipulation. No legitimate dev / review / test workflow loads or unloads modules.
Kernel boot / panic / reboot surface. kexec swaps the running kernel image; reboot panics the host.
Filesystem mount surface. Mounting/unmounting + pivot_root + chroot are how container escapes most often happen. Coder can cd / read / write within the existing tree but cannot remap it.
Privilege boundary changes. setuid/setgid escalation paths plus capability set manipulation that would let the sandbox grow root-equivalent rights.
Hostname / domain / time / clock control. Lets an attacker mask telemetry timestamps or fool name-resolution.
Block / character device IO control beyond the file API. ioperm / iopl give direct port access; bpf can install eBPF programs the sandbox shouldn't ship.
User namespace creation. Required for nested containers; an LLM that generates a Dockerfile + `docker build` inside the sandbox should fail loudly rather than escape.
Filesystem swap toggling. swapon / swapoff are root-only on Linux but explicitly denied here so a CAP_SYS_ADMIN run still fails closed.
Quotactl + filesystem freeze. Sandbox processes don't manage quotas; freeze is a denial-of-service primitive against the host filesystem.
Kernel keyring + audit. add_key / keyctl manipulate kernel-resident credentials; auditctl masks tracing.
